name: Slate
maturity: Core-wiki first-release candidate. Advanced flagship systems remain outside the first public release acceptance.

spine.record: a page in a tree in a container

description: One home for everything your team knows: pages, databases and search.
scope: One business, one workspace; complete inherited knowledge workspace plus all six journeys, full flagship and sustained inquiry. Requirements are not acceptance evidence.

capabilities.description: An installed Slate answers the root with the shared Lobby (Finish setup until first-run setup is finished, then Sign in) and Base's /setup/state; the static landing page is the run site's homepage (run-slate.com), around the owner's name and description beside Slate's card logo (the same card mark the sign-in page, the app and the favicon use), with Run Slate to /run, a Docs link to /docs, "Read the guide" to /docs and "Read the setup guide" to /docs/install, a link to the source repository, one illustrated section for each core-wiki capability it names, and an optional static credit.

First-party public documentation at /docs: the repository Markdown that docs/site.json publishes, rendered to HTML at build time by a Vite plugin, in the landing's own header, footer and type, describing only the default core-wiki profile.
One workspace with roles, groups, guests, invitations, an identity-provider adapter, settings, theme and first run, and visible sign-in and invitation mail delivery.
Durable save, revision conflicts, idempotent mutations, recovery and optional real co-editing with current access.
The primary record: identity that survives every move, creation, duplication, icon and cover, details and owner, favourite, watch, outline, present, display options, analytics and reactions.
A nested tree per container with explicit ordering, a shared-with-me list, a per-container title filter, and create in place.
A block editor: typed reorderable blocks, inline text, the insert menu, Markdown shortcuts, mentions, structured blocks, task items, media, safe link cards and live content queries.
Draft, scheduled, live and unpublished-changes states over one model, a draft that is private whatever the profile, and a lifecycle profile that follows either incumbent.
Grants to people, groups, containers and the workspace at four levels, inheritance and restriction, general access, guest invitations, immediate revocation and expiring grants.
Anonymous reading that takes two acts and an ungated container veto, a stored slug and theme, a chrome-free read view, no inherited publishing, indexing off by default, and immediate unpublish.
Content-hashed immutable revisions, readable history, restore, compare, citations that resolve to the revision they name, version deletion, and a numbered or snapshot profile.

A workspace status vocabulary, one status per page, verification by someone who opened the revision, honest lapse, an open-vocabulary or verification-only profile, and nightly container verification rules that flag or unverify, never verify.
Anchored and page threads, authorship-bound editing, mentions, anchors that survive edits, reactions, a discussions panel and resolve.
Archive with restore, a trash nothing leaves on a timer, and explicit permanent deletion with tombstones.
Containers with visibility, grants and external-access switches, creation from a purpose, an index, their own settings shell, personal containers, bulk actions and an access profile.
Databases in the same tree: typed fields, named views, layouts, filters, grouping, calculations, charts, structure locks, embedded views, and a record that is a page or a row.
Rules that run as their actor, never exceed that member's access, keep a run log, are bounded against loops, and scope to a source, a container or the site.
Ranked search over retained text with filters, freshness, a permission boundary that hides existence, container scope, honest empty results, and results without AI.
Home, recents, favourites, one navigation whose order is data, global create, and a touch client that edits rather than reads.
An in-app inbox for mentions, comments, watched pages, grants and lapsed verifications, and an optional chat destination that carries a link rather than content.
An append-only, access-filtered timeline of member, automation and AI work that survives deletion of what it describes.
A searchable gallery, honest previews, snapshot on use, custom templates, saving a page as one, and workspace or container scope.
Rolled-back, reported, idempotent import jobs, one importer for each incumbent's own export, safe extraction, and document import into a page.

A complete workspace export, referential restore, visible jobs, rebuilt search, an access boundary on import, atomic import, page and container archives, and reader-authorized Word page/descendant export with optional comments and merged-table/image-alt re-import.
Permanent URLs, tombstones, references that follow their target, and links that reveal nothing about a record the reader may not open.
Cited scoped AI, proposals or explicitly granted effects, durable staged runs and owner-bounded budgets with current requester/audience checks.
A decision layer over a page: states, an editable proposal, an immutable accepted record with citations to revisions, a filterable log and review dates.
Anchored suggestions; Resolve explicitly. Requirements pending acceptance.
Connector contract; Exact passages; Scoped claims and authority; Live observations; Revocation and deletion; Credential lifecycle. Requirements pending acceptance.
Versioned procedure; Evaluation and activation; Version transitions. Requirements pending acceptance.
Durable effects; Consent and product custody; Impact and maintenance. Requirements pending acceptance.
Semantic parity; Portable owner interfaces. Requirements pending acceptance.
Open questions; Reproducible reasoning; Bounded planning; Routing and ambient discovery; Economical sustained work. Requirements pending acceptance.
Predeclared comparison; Exposure and safety; Outcome classification; Reusable learning. Requirements pending acceptance.
Complete product gate; Independent evidence; Value and held-out evaluation; Complete portable knowledge. Requirements pending acceptance.
Assigned page tasks, per-reader task reports, personal task lists and durable timezone-aware inbox reminders.
Permission-aware advanced queries, saved-search content blocks, verification-aware ranking, trust badges and near-duplicate grouping.
Durable page opt-outs, personal and workspace autowatch settings, container watches and permission-aware Home Following.
Dated, attributed space blog posts with permission-aware space and Home feeds, follower notices and Confluence Cloud blog import.
Readable workspace, container and page archives preserve authored discussions, reply relationships, resolved states and inline anchors through re-import.
Click-to-load allowlisted design, video and document embeds in isolated provider frames.

Owner-configured nightly or weekly S3-compatible/R2 backups with verified retention, encrypted destination credentials, in-app failures and empty-deployment restore drill instructions. Real bucket acceptance remains pending.

Member-delegated Google Drive and SharePoint folder previews and private page-tree imports with resolving document links and retained per-file omission reports. Real provider acceptance remains pending.

Owner-configured signed SAML SP and IdP sign-in, DNS-verified invited or allow-listed admission, enforced member SSO, guest email access and one designated owner break-glass path. Real provider acceptance remains pending.
Wiki curator MCP jobs, classes, resources, events and a seeded week under the company’s held and all-autonomous policies; no completed conformance journey is claimed.
The complete retained wiki and inquiry target; planned registration is not acceptance or a release.

nonGoals: Plan ladders, subscription trials, credits, seat counting, and in-product upgrade paths: one product with every feature on has nothing to gate.
A vendor product shelf, app switcher, or cross-product chrome from a suite this product is not part of.
A commercial marketplace or storefront of templates, apps, agents, or services; the extension surface ships and the shop does not.
Deep coupling to one issue tracker: an issue URL is a link card like any other.
A bundled screen recorder: a recording is a media block.
More than one workspace or tenant per deployment.
A native mobile application: the operator app is one responsive web application, and it edits rather than reads on touch.

externals.why: The supported deployment target supplies Worker compute, D1 records and search, R2 files and media, and Queues for import, export and automation jobs.
data: Every page, record, comment, file and activity entry in the deployment
Member email addresses and session identifiers
Anonymous readers' requests to published pages

externals.why: Resend sends magic-link sign-in, member invitations and guest invitations through the mail.sender.v1 adapter; Cloudflare's owned primitives do not send hosted email.
data: The recipient's email address
The workspace name and the inviting member's display name
A single-use sign-in or invitation URL

externals.why: Selection editing, summaries, workspace answers and agents require model inference, which no owned primitive provides.
data: The member's instruction or question
The text of the pages and revisions the run is scoped to, which the asking member may already read
Record identifiers used to cite the answer
Authorized connected-source passages, skill procedures, inquiry context and experiment evidence included in the asking member-readable evidence packet

externals.why: Sign-in through the buyer's own identity provider cannot be served by the deployment's native session auth, which remains the default.
data: The signing-in member's email address
The authentication request and its returned assertion

externals.requiredWhen: LINK_PREVIEWS_ENABLED=true and a member pastes a URL
externals.why: A link card shows the target's own title, description and icon, which only the target origin can supply; no owned primitive can know them.
data: The URL a member pasted, sent to that URL's own origin
The deployment's outbound IP address and user agent

externals.requiredWhen: a workspace or container owner connects a chat destination
externals.why: Delivering a notification into the buyer's chat tool requires that tool's own API; nothing owned can post into it.
data: The event name and the actor's display name
The page title and a link to it, never the page body

externals.requiredWhen: An owner connects Google Docs, Slack, GitHub, HappyToHelp or Orbit, or grants a supported provider effect
externals.why: Configured provider APIs perform identity, current authorization, evidence reads and explicitly granted effects. Native HappyToHelp and Orbit use owner-configured exact origins and expiring delegated accounts. Local adapter checks do not establish live provider acceptance.
data: Provider token sent only to its provider API
Selected source identifiers and authenticated principal/account
Authorized GitHub issue title/body/state for an explicitly granted update
OAuth authorization code, PKCE verifier and configured client identity sent only to the selected provider token endpoint
Native HappyToHelp article content/status and Orbit handoff content, exact targets, audience and operation receipt identifiers for explicitly granted effects

externals.requiredWhen: LINK_PREVIEWS_ENABLED=true and a member requests a link preview
externals.why: Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS resolves the pasted hostname before public-address validation and each redirect.
data: The pasted URL hostname and record types A and AAAA, sent to cloudflare-dns.com
The deployment outbound IP address

externals.why: Slate's SendGrid adapter sends sign-in and invitation links; uncertain acceptance is held for provider review without automatic resubmission.
data: The recipient's email address
The workspace name and the inviting member's display name
A single-use sign-in or invitation URL

externals.requiredWhen: A reader chooses Load for an allowlisted Figma, Miro, Lucid, Loom, YouTube, Vimeo, Google Docs/Sheets/Slides or Microsoft 365 embed
externals.why: The provider serves its interactive document or video in its own sandboxed frame after the reader explicitly requests it. Slate cannot serve the provider application itself.
data: The provider resource URL and identifier
The reader IP address, browser request headers and provider-owned cookies permitted by the browser, only after interaction
No Slate page body, Slate session cookie or referrer is sent to the provider

externals.requiredWhen: an authenticated member opens a readable page containing an allowlisted provider embed
externals.why: Provider response headers and explicit refusal documents determine whether a click-to-load embed must become its original link card. Published readers never trigger a server-side provider read.
data: The allowlisted provider embed URL, sent anonymously to an allowlisted provider endpoint
The deployment outbound IP address and user agent; no member credentials, cookies or visitor data

deploy.notes: The root is the shared Lobby (HOME-001, amended 13 October 2026; the static landing page is the run site's homepage at run-slate.com): matched exactly, it shows Finish setup or Sign in from the first-run record alone, lists no workspace content, sets no cookie, runs no script and loads only same-origin resources. /setup/state is Base's exact claimed-or-unclaimed answer from the same reading, with no session, no cookie and no-store. /docs is the first-party documentation (DOCS-001, 9 October 2026): the exact path and everything under /docs/ are public build-time documents that read no workspace record, set no cookie and load only same-origin resources, behind the same configuration gate and public-document rate limit as the landing; an unknown slug is a 404. The favicon files (/favicon.svg, /favicon-32.png, /favicon.ico, /apple-touch-icon.png) are fixed same-origin static files of Slate's card mark; /rer-theme.css (the landing's colours, Outfit and radius, read by the shared confirmation page and the Lobby and linked by /signin and /setup), /slate-mark.svg (the same mark, light only) and /brand/band.svg (the Lobby's floor art) are three more. /p/ serves published pages: a path under it resolves only while that page's public exposure record is live and its container permits public links, and returns a content-free page otherwise. Everything else, including /app and every workspace data endpoint, requires a session. /_serverFn/ is TanStack Start's generated transport and is not a public path: each private handler validates the native session itself before any private read or mutation, and an anonymous call receives the framework's serialized denial with no product payload. The exact /auth/confirm route is a Hono-owned server-rendered native email confirmation: GET only previews; same-origin POST consumes a new token and creates the session. It shares configuration and auth rate checks. Other /auth paths remain ordinary unmatched documents. Previously issued /api/auth/magic/accept links return the request-new-link page.
